questions.stem: What is the functional group in carboxylic acids?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH (carboxyl) functional group. This group is responsible for the acidic properties and characteristic reactions of carboxylic acids.

questions.stem: Ethanoic acid is found in vinegar. What is its chemical formula?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid has the formula CH₃COOH. It is a weak acid commonly found in vinegar (approximately 5% solution).

questions.stem: How do carboxylic acids compare to strong mineral acids like hydrochloric acid?

options.text: They are exactly the same strength
They are weak acids that only partially ionise in water
They are not acids at all

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids are weak acids. They only partially dissociate in water, releasing fewer H⁺ ions than a strong acid at the same concentration, so they have a higher pH.

questions.stem: What is produced when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate?

options.text: Sodium ethanoate, water, and carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates just like mineral acids: ethanoic acid + sodium carbonate → sodium ethanoate + water + carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: What is the name of the simplest carboxylic acid?
questions.explanation: Methanoic acid (HCOOH) is the simplest carboxylic acid with just one carbon atom. It is also known as formic acid and is found naturally in ant stings.

questions.stem: Carboxylic acids react with alcohols to produce:
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with alcohols in a condensation reaction called esterification to produce an ester and water, in the presence of an acid catalyst.

questions.stem: Carboxylic acids dissolve in water to form acidic solutions. Why is this?

options.text: The -COOH group partially ionises to release H⁺ ions
They react with water to form hydrogen gas

questions.explanation: The -COOH group can donate a hydrogen ion (H⁺) to water, making the solution acidic. Because only some molecules ionise, they are weak acids with a pH typically between 3 and 6.
